# `ui-provider`

Setting display defaults, theme, density and scale for the app or a subtree.

## Selection

- **Use when:** Setting display defaults, theme, density and scale for the app or a subtree.
- **Avoid when:** The value is per-feature policy or domain data, which stays a prop.
- **Consider instead:** `features/theme-tweaker`
- **Stability:** stable.

## Import

```tsx fragment — import-only example
import { CSPProvider } from "themelia-ui/ui-provider"
```

## Composition

This family has no component-family dependencies.

Application policy—routing, fetching, persistence, permissions, and translation—stays
outside the package and arrives through the public props, callbacks, slots, or accessors below.

### `configToAttributes`

Kind: callable.

Attributes the stylesheet keys off. Density is an attribute, not a variable, so the
preset values stay in styles/tokens/foundation.css and a bare `data-density` works too.

```text
(config: UIConfig) => Record<string, string | undefined>
```

### `configToCssVars`

Kind: callable.

Translates the token-bearing half of a config into CSS custom properties, returned as a
style object for the scope's own element so nesting merges through the cascade.

The rule: a value that can be a token is CSS; a decision a component makes in JavaScript
stays in context. Nothing appears in both.

```text
(config: UIConfig) => Record<string, string>
```

Supply the request's nonce when inline elements are allowed by nonce, or set

Extends: `Pick<BaseCSPProviderProps, "children" | "nonce" | "disableStyleElements">`.

### `Scope`

Kind: callable.

`<Scope>` — a token boundary without the config machinery. Derived tokens re-compute
only at a scope boundary (styles/SCOPES.md), so a factor set on a plain `div` changes
nothing; this renders `data-ui-scope`. Use `<UIProvider>` when JavaScript config changes too.

  <Scope vars={{ "--density-scale": 0.8 }}>
    <Toolbar />
  </Scope>

```text
({ vars, as: Tag, transparent, className, style, children, }: { vars: Record<string, string | number>; as?: ElementType; transparent?: boolean; className?: string; style?: CSSProperties; children: ReactNode; }) => import("react").JSX.Element
```

### `TextSize`

Kind: type.

Step on the type scale. `inherit` lets the surrounding size flow through.

```text
"inherit" | "xxs" | "xs" | "pxs" | "sm" | "base" | "lg" | "xl"
```

### `ThemeConfig`

Kind: interface.

Theme overrides. Token names are generated from the stylesheet, so a typo is a type error.

| member | required | type | description / documented default |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `radius` | no | `string` | The container radius — cards, dialogs, popovers, menus. Writes `--radius`. |
| `radiusSm` | no | `string` | The inner radius — controls, rows, chips, badges, tooltips. Writes `--radius-sm`.<br>Not derived from `radius`: set both. |
| `colors` | no | `Partial<Record<SemanticToken, string>>` | Semantic colour overrides. Prefer these to `palette`. |
| `palette` | no | `Partial<Record<PaletteToken, string>>` | Primitive ramp overrides: moves every semantic resolving through the step. |
| `vars` | no | `Record<string, string>` | Escape hatch for custom properties the kit does not define. Keys omit `--`. |

Kind: interface.

| member | required | type | description / documented default |

### `UIPortalContainer`

Kind: type.

Where a popup should render so it keeps its scope. Theme and density inherit down the
DOM, so popups portal into an element inside the scope rather than `document.body`.

```text
HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null
```

### `UIPortalHost`

Kind: callable.

Keeps popups inside this subtree, so they inherit the scope's custom properties and
`[data-density]` / `[data-theme]` attributes instead of the root's.

```tsx fragment — declaration JSDoc excerpt
<UIScope config={{ density: "compact", colorScheme: "dark" }}>
  <UIPortalHost>
    <DropdownMenu>…</DropdownMenu>
  </UIPortalHost>
</UIScope>
```

Opt-in per region; without a host, popups portal to the document as usual.

```text
({ container, children }: UIPortalHostProps) => import("react").JSX.Element
```

### `UIProvider`

Kind: callable.

`<UIProvider>` — composes `UIRoot` and `UIScope`: outermost, a root that themes
`documentElement` plus a scope; nested, a scope only. Prefer `UIRoot` and `UIScope`
directly, which let a root decline the document.

```text
({ config, transparent, className, style, children }: UIProviderProps) => import("react").JSX.Element
```

### `UIProviderProps`

Kind: interface.

| member | required | type | description / documented default |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `config` | no | `UIConfig` | Merged over the enclosing provider, or over the library defaults at the root. |
| `transparent` | no | `boolean` | Removes the wrapper from layout with `display: contents`; custom properties still<br>inherit. Set `false` when the scope should be a real box, such as a themed panel. |
| `className` | no | `string` |  |
| `style` | no | `CSSProperties` |  |
| `children` | yes | `ReactNode` |  |

### `UIRoot`

Kind: callable.

`<UIRoot>` — the application's configuration, once. Renders no element; region scoping
is `UIScope`, which does.

```text
({ config, documentTarget, children }: UIRootProps) => import("react").JSX.Element
```

### `UIRootProps`

Kind: interface.

| member | required | type | description / documented default |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `config` | no | `UIConfig` | The application's defaults. Merged over the library's own. |
| `documentTarget` | no | `UIDocumentTarget` | Which element gets the theme and density attributes, or `false` (default) for none.<br>Opt-in because it writes outside the tree, which could fight another root or an app's<br>own `data-theme`; it is the only way a root can theme the page canvas. |
| `children` | yes | `ReactNode` |  |

### `UIScope`

Kind: callable.

`<UIScope>` — a region with its own tokens. Nests freely; writes only its own custom
property overrides and never touches the document. `render` picks the element, e.g.
`<UIScope render={<aside />}>`, for places a `div` is invalid.

```text
({ config, transparent, render, className, style, ...props }: UIScopeProps) => import("react").JSX.Element
```

### `UIScopeProps`

Kind: interface.

Extends: `useRender.ComponentProps<"div">`.

| member | required | type | description / documented default |
| --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| `config` | no | `UIConfig` | Merged over the nearest enclosing scope or root. |
| `transparent` | no | `boolean` | Removes the element from layout with `display: contents`; custom properties still<br>inherit. Set `false` when the scope should be a real box, such as a themed panel. |

## Preview recipes

Preview route: Dropdown & context menu — `/dropdown-menu`

### Dark by default, decided by the provider

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIProvider config={{ overlay: { darkMenus: false } }}>
  <App />
</UIProvider>
```

### Scale

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<Scope vars={{ "--density-scale": 0.875 }}>…</Scope>
```

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIProvider config={{ defaults: { sheet: { size: "26rem", inset: true } } }}>
```

### In another language

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
import { de } from "date-fns/locale"

<UIProvider config={{ dates: { locale: de } }}>…</UIProvider>

{/* or hand the wording over completely */}
<UIProvider
  config={{ dates: { formatRelativeTime: (date, now) => t.relative(date, now) } }}
/>
```

### The factor

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIProvider config={{ scale: 0.875 }}>
  <Toolbar />
</UIProvider>
```

### Why not size props

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
{/* smaller type, control geometry untouched */}
<UIProvider config={{ typography: { scale: 0.875 } }}>…</UIProvider>

{/* denser geometry, type held at its default */}
<UIProvider config={{ scale: 0.875, typography: { scale: 1 } }}>…</UIProvider>
```

### Two levels of control

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
/* everything denser */
<UIProvider config={{ scale: 0.875 }}>

/* heights and rows only — gaps untouched */
<Scope vars={{ "--density-scale": 0.875 }}>

/* gaps and padding only — control heights untouched */
<Scope vars={{ "--density-scale": 0.875 }}>

/* one measurement, leaving everything else alone */
<Scope vars={{ "--button-h": "2.75rem" }}>

/* a plain div does NOT work: overriding a factor needs a scope
   boundary, or the measurements above it have already resolved. */
```

### Why two factors, and no third

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIProvider config={{ scale: 1.125 }}>
  <Page>
    <UIProvider config={{ scale: 0.875 }}>
      <Toolbar />
    </UIProvider>
  </Page>
</UIProvider>
```

### Density presets

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIProvider config={{ density: "compact" }}>…</UIProvider>

{/* or, with no provider at all */}
<div data-density="compact">…</div>
```

### Semantic tier

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIProvider config={{ theme: { colors: { primary: "oklch(0.55 0.2 25)" } } }}>
```

### A scope is a region

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIScope config={{ density: "compact" }}>
  <Toolbar />
</UIScope>
```

### Nesting merges

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIScope config={{ colorScheme: "dark" }}>
  <UIScope config={{ density: "compact" }}>…</UIScope>
</UIScope>
```

### render decides the element

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIScope render={<aside />} config={{ density: "compact" }}>…</UIScope>
```

### Popups stay inside the scope

```tsx fragment — excerpt from the live preview; surrounding values are supplied by the application
<UIScope config={{ density: "compact" }}>
  <UIPortalHost>
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button>Actions</Button>} />
      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuItem>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  </UIPortalHost>
</UIScope>
```
